source: Written 2026-10-23/24 by Claude Sonnet from our own summaries of the NC 2017 standards, and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin.

notes.NC17.5.OA.2: Whole-number expressions with parentheses and brackets (no braces, since the converter has no \{). Skills: evaluate, write from words, interpret without evaluating, properties, two-step word problems, equivalent expressions, missing number. A student cannot be asked to "explain" in text, so explaining is tested as choosing the right statement. Wrote 69 (23 per difficulty), whole numbers only. Braces are avoided; brackets and parentheses are used for grouping. Mixed expressions without grouping appear only where multiplication or division inside a term is unambiguous.
notes.NC17.5.OA.3: Plots are described in words (no pictures): reading and plotting ordered pairs, moves between points, and which point lies on a pattern graph. All terms are whole numbers in the first quadrant; rules are additive, with multiples appearing as relationships between matching terms.
notes.NC17.5.NBT.1: 30 questions written. Skills: place value relationships 5, multiply by powers of ten 6, divide by powers of ten 6, exponent form of powers of ten 6, value of a digit 3, explaining the pattern 4. Negative exponents are left out (not Grade 5).
notes.NC17.5.NBT.5: Whole-number products only; the largest factors are 3-digit by 2-digit, as the standard says. Skills (rough counts): two-digit by two-digit 4, three-digit by two-digit 6, partial products 6, multiply by a multiple of ten 3, word problems 6, estimate to check 3, missing digit 2. Written work in columns is described by its rows (partial products) in words. Products only, as the standard asks; no division. Money is avoided (no dollar sign).
notes.NC17.5.NBT.6: All 69 written, 23 per difficulty; nothing left out.
notes.NC17.5.NBT.7: Decimals are kept to hundredths (products of two tenths reach hundredths); models and drawings are described in words rather than shown. Division of a decimal by a decimal uses friendly numbers that divide exactly.
notes.NC17.5.NF.1: Denominators are always related (one a multiple of the other) so the common denominator is the larger; answers are fractions or mixed numbers. Choice answers have no compute because the checker accepts only plain numbers there; keys were verified by exact fraction arithmetic in the generator. Denominators are related (one is a multiple of the other: halves, fourths, eighths; thirds and sixths; fifths and tenths; twelfths). Covers adding and subtracting fractions and mixed numbers (with regrouping), word problems, estimating with benchmarks, finding a missing part or start, renaming to a common denominator and finding mistakes. Numeric answers say when simplest form or a mixed number is wanted.
notes.NC17.5.NF.3: Whole-number answers are avoided; answers are fractions or mixed numbers, as in the standard. Skills (rough counts): fraction as numerator divided by denominator (6), share less than 1 (5), share a mixed number (6), size of a quotient (4), find the amount shared (2), compare shares (2), match a story to a division (2), two-step sharing (2), find the error (1). Decimal answers left out on purpose.
notes.NC17.5.NF.4: Area and length models are described in words (rows and columns, a rectangle with fractional sides). Answers that are fractions are in simplest form where the stem says so; any equivalent form is accepted.
notes.NC17.5.MD.1: The conversion fact is always given in the question, as with a conversion chart, so no fact has to be remembered; both customary and metric systems, and time. Almost all are larger unit to smaller unit by multiplying; one item (60 inches to feet) goes the other way and is worded as "what number times 12 makes 60". No conversion between customary and metric. Skills (rough counts): customary lengths 4, metric lengths 3, weight or mass 4, capacity 4, time 2, decimal measures 3, convert then add/subtract/compare 7, choose or explain the conversion 2, small unit to large unit 1.
notes.NC17.5.MD.4: Pictures of cube stacks are written as layers, rows and towers. Cubic-centimeter and cubic-foot units appear only to name the unit; volume of a rectangular prism by formula (NC.5.MD.5) is not asked.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: What is the value of $(6 + 4) \times 3$?
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $6 + 4 = 10$. Then $10 \times 3 = 30$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression shows "add 5 and 3, then multiply by 2"?
questions.solution: The adding is done first, so it goes in parentheses: $(5 + 3) \times 2 = 16$.

solve.work: Add 5 and 3 first, then multiply by 2: (5 + 3) x 2.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $20 - (8 + 4)$.
questions.solution: Parentheses first: $8 + 4 = 12$. Then $20 - 12 = 8$.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Which expression is 4 times as large as $9 + 2$?
questions.solution: To make $9 + 2$ four times as large, multiply the whole sum by 4: $4 \times (9 + 2)$.

solve.work: 4 times as large as (9+2) is 4 x (9 + 2).

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: Tom has 3 bags with 5 marbles in each bag. Then he gets 4 more marbles. How many marbles does he have now?
questions.solution: The bags hold $3 \times 5 = 15$ marbles. Adding 4 more gives $15 + 4 = 19$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: What is the value of $(8 + 4) \div 2$?
questions.solution: Parentheses first: $8 + 4 = 12$. Then $12 \div 2 = 6$. (Dividing only the 4 gives the wrong value 10.)

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the commutative property to find the ? in $4 + 7 = 7 + ?$.
questions.solution: Numbers can be added in either order and the sum stays the same, so the ? is 4.

questions.skill: Equivalent expressions
questions.stem: Which expression has the same value as $(2 + 3) \times 4$?
questions.solution: $(2 + 3) \times 4 = 5 \times 4 = 20$. The others have values 14, 11 and 9.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $30 \div (2 + 3)$.
questions.solution: Parentheses first: $2 + 3 = 5$. Then $30 \div 5 = 6$.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Which words match $3 \times (4 + 5)$?
questions.solution: The parentheses group $4 + 5$ as one number, and 3 multiplies all of it: 3 times the sum of 4 and 5.

solve.work: 3 x (4+5) is 3 times the sum of 4 and 5.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Evaluate $(9 - 4) \times 6$.
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $9 - 4 = 5$. Then $5 \times 6 = 30$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Compute $3 \times (5 + 2)$.
questions.solution: Parentheses first: $5 + 2 = 7$. Then $3 \times 7 = 21$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Work out $(12 + 8) \div 4$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: Jo buys 3 packs of 4 pens and 2 single pens. How many pens does Jo buy in all?
questions.solution: $3 \times 4 = 12$ pens in the packs, and $12 + 2 = 14$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: Marta has 15 stickers. She gives 3 stickers to each of 4 friends. How many stickers does she have left?
questions.solution: She gives away $4 \times 3 = 12$ stickers. $15 - 12 = 3$ are left.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the commutative property to find the ? in $6 \times 9 = ? \times 6$. What is the ?
questions.solution: Factors can be swapped: $6 \times 9 = 9 \times 6$. The ? is 9.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the associative property to find the ? in $(2 + 5) + 8 = 2 + (? + 8)$. What is the ?
questions.solution: The numbers keep their order and only the grouping changes, so the ? is 5.

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: What number makes $(? + 3) \times 2 = 14$ true?
questions.solution: $14 \div 2 = 7$, so $? + 3 = 7$ and the number is 4. Check: $(4 + 3) \times 2 = 14$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the distributive property to find the ? in $4 \times (10 + 2) = 4 \times 10 + 4 \times ?$. What is the ?
questions.solution: The 4 multiplies both 10 and 2, so the ? is 2.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Calculate $18 \div (2 + 1)$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: A movie ticket costs 8 dollars. Ben buys 2 tickets and pays with a 20 dollar bill. How many dollars of change does he get?
questions.solution: Two tickets cost $2 \times 8 = 16$ dollars. $20 - 16 = 4$ dollars of change.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression shows "multiply 4 by the sum of 2 and 6"?
questions.solution: The sum $2 + 6$ must be found first, so it goes in parentheses and is multiplied by 4.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Which words match $(7 - 2) \times 5$?
choices: 5 less than the product of 7 and 2
questions.solution: The parentheses hold $7 - 2$, the difference of 7 and 2, and that is multiplied by 5.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Which expression has a value of 24?
questions.solution: $(3 + 5) \times 3 = 8 \times 3 = 24$. The others are 18, 11 and 12.

questions.skill: Equivalent expressions
questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $9 + (4 + 1)$?
questions.solution: Both equal 14: grouping of addition does not change the sum (associative property). The others equal 12, 45 and 12.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Which property is shown by $5 \times 8 = 8 \times 5$?
questions.solution: Changing the order of the factors without changing the product is the commutative property.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Lena has 3 boxes with 6 apples in each box. She eats 2 apples. Which expression shows how many apples are left?
questions.solution: She starts with $3 \times 6 = 18$ apples and eats 2, so $18 - 2 = 16$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression means "add 10 and 4, then subtract 3"?
questions.solution: Add first, $10 + 4 = 14$, then subtract 3 to get 11.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: What is the value of $24 \div (4 + 2)$?
questions.solution: Parentheses first: $4 + 2 = 6$. Then $24 \div 6 = 4$.

questions.skill: Equivalent expressions
questions.stem: Which expression equals $7 \times 6$ when 6 is written as $5 + 1$?
questions.solution: $7 \times (5 + 1) = 7 \times 5 + 7 \times 1 = 35 + 7 = 42$ (distributive property).

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: Which number is the ? in $(4 + 5) \times 3 = 4 \times 3 + ? \times 3$?
questions.solution: The 3 multiplies each number in $(4 + 5)$, so the ? is 5.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Three notebooks cost 4 dollars each and one pen costs 2 dollars. Which expression shows the total cost in dollars?
questions.solution: The notebooks cost $3 \times 4$ and the pen adds 2.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $[18 - (3 \times 4)] \times 2$.
questions.solution: Work from the inside out: $3 \times 4 = 12$, then $18 - 12 = 6$, then $6 \times 2 = 12$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $7 \times (15 - 9) + 8$.
questions.solution: Parentheses first: $15 - 9 = 6$. Then $7 \times 6 = 42$. Then $42 + 8 = 50$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: A baker makes 5 trays of 12 rolls and then sells 18 rolls. Which expression gives the number of rolls left?
questions.solution: The baker makes $5 \times 12$ rolls and sells 18, so $5 \times 12 - 18 = 60 - 18 = 42$ rolls are left.

solve.work: 5 trays of 12 = 5 x 12 = 60, minus 18 sold: 5 x 12 - 18 = 42.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Which expression equals $6 \times 27$ when the distributive property is used?
questions.solution: Break 27 into $20 + 7$. Then $6 \times 27 = 6 \times 20 + 6 \times 7 = 120 + 42 = 162$.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the properties of operations to find the value of $25 \times 7 \times 4$.
questions.solution: Multiply in a friendlier order: $25 \times 4 = 100$, then $100 \times 7 = 700$.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Which statement is true about $5 \times (200 + 14)$, without finding its value?
choices: It is 5 times as large as $200 + 14$.
It is 5 times as large as 200, plus 14.
questions.answer: It is 5 times as large as $200 + 14$.
questions.solution: The 5 multiplies the whole sum in parentheses, so the value is 5 times as large as $200 + 14$.

solve.answer: It is 5 times as large as $200 + 14$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: Carlos has 45 dollars. He buys 3 books that cost 8 dollars each. How many dollars does he have left?
questions.solution: The books cost $3 \times 8 = 24$ dollars. Carlos has $45 - 24 = 21$ dollars left.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression shows "subtract 6 from 20, then divide by 7"?
questions.solution: The subtraction is done first, so it goes in parentheses: $(20 - 6) \div 7 = 14 \div 7 = 2$.

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: What number makes $4 \times (9 + ?) = 52$ true?
questions.solution: Since $4 \times 13 = 52$, the parentheses must equal 13. Then $9 + ? = 13$, so the ? is 4.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Which expression has a value of 18?
questions.solution: $(4 + 5) \times 2 = 9 \times 2 = 18$. The others are 14, 11 and 12.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Evaluate $(45 - 9) \div 6 + 7$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $12 \times (8 + 17)$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: Evaluate $[(20 - 8) \times 3] - 5$.
questions.solution: Inside first: $20 - 8 = 12$. Then $12 \times 3 = 36$. Then $36 - 5 = 31$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $5 \times [30 - (4 \times 6)]$.
questions.solution: Innermost first: $4 \times 6 = 24$. Then $30 - 24 = 6$. Then $5 \times 6 = 30$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: A theater has 12 rows with 8 seats in each row. 25 seats are taken. How many seats are empty?
questions.solution: There are $12 \times 8 = 96$ seats. $96 - 25 = 71$ are empty.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: Sam buys 4 shirts at 9 dollars each and a hat for 12 dollars. How many dollars does he spend in all?
questions.solution: Shirts: $4 \times 9 = 36$. Total: $36 + 12 = 48$ dollars.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the properties of operations to find the value of $2 \times 17 \times 5$.
questions.solution: Multiply 2 and 5 first: $2 \times 5 = 10$. Then $10 \times 17 = 170$.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the distributive property, writing 103 as $100 + 3$, to find $6 \times 103$.

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: What number makes $(? - 6) \times 5 = 35$ true?
questions.solution: $35 \div 5 = 7$, so $? - 6 = 7$ and the number is 13. Check: $(13 - 6) \times 5 = 35$.

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: What number makes $60 \div (? + 2) = 6$ true?
questions.solution: $60 \div 6 = 10$, so $? + 2 = 10$ and the number is 8.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $(9 + 15) \div (2 + 4)$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression shows "divide 36 by the sum of 4 and 5"?
questions.solution: The sum $4 + 5$ is the divisor, so it needs parentheses: $36 \div (4 + 5) = 4$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Two friends each buy 3 tickets that cost 7 dollars each. Which expression shows the total cost in dollars?
questions.solution: Each friend pays $3 \times 7$, and there are 2 friends: $2 \times (3 \times 7) = 42$ dollars.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Which expression is 10 more than the product of 4 and 6?
questions.solution: The product $4 \times 6$ comes first, then 10 is added.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Which words match $(8 + 12) \div 5$?
choices: 5 divided by the sum of 8 and 12
the difference of 8 and 12, divided by 5
the sum of 8 and 12, divided by 5
questions.answer: the sum of 8 and 12, divided by 5
questions.solution: The parentheses hold the sum of 8 and 12, and that sum is divided by 5.

solve.answer: the sum of 8 and 12, divided by 5

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Which equation shows the associative property?
questions.solution: The associative property changes only the grouping of the numbers. The other equations show the commutative property, the distributive property and multiplying by 1.

questions.skill: Equivalent expressions
questions.stem: Which expression has the same value as $2 \times 9 \times 5$?
questions.solution: Multiplication can be done in any order and grouping: $2 \times 9 \times 5 = 90 = (2 \times 5) \times 9$. The others equal 63, 23 and 28.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses
questions.stem: Which expression has the greatest value?
questions.solution: The values are 42, 40, 16 and 17.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: What is the value of $[(7 + 5) \times 2] - (3 \times 4)$?

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: Which number makes $5 \times (? + 3) = 40$ true?

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: A farm has 7 cows and 9 sheep. Each animal eats 3 pounds of feed. Which expression shows the total pounds of feed?
questions.solution: There are $7 + 9$ animals and each eats 3 pounds, so $(7 + 9) \times 3 = 48$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Jill has 50 dollars and buys 2 books that cost 12 dollars each. Which expression shows how many dollars she has left?
questions.solution: The books cost $2 \times 12 = 24$ dollars. Subtract that from 50: 26 dollars left.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Why is $3 \times (4 + 6)$ equal to $3 \times 4 + 3 \times 6$?
choices: The 3 multiplies only the 4 in the parentheses.
Addition and multiplication can be done in any order.
The 3 multiplies each number inside the parentheses.
questions.answer: The 3 multiplies each number inside the parentheses.
questions.solution: Both equal 30. The distributive property says the multiplier applies to each addend.

solve.answer: The 3 multiplies each number inside the parentheses.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $4 \times [(6 + 2) \times 3 - 10]$.
questions.solution: Inside the brackets, the parentheses first: $6 + 2 = 8$. Then $8 \times 3 = 24$, and $24 - 10 = 14$. Finally $4 \times 14 = 56$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $2 \times [40 - (7 \times 4)] + 15$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Dana buys 3 shirts for 12 dollars each and 2 hats for 9 dollars each. She pays with a 100 dollar bill. Which expression gives her change in dollars?
questions.solution: The shirts cost $3 \times 12$ and the hats cost $2 \times 9$. Both costs are taken from 100, so the sum goes in parentheses: $100 - (36 + 18) = 46$ dollars.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: A school buys 6 boxes of 24 pencils. It gives 4 classes 15 pencils each. How many pencils are left?
questions.solution: The school buys $6 \times 24 = 144$ pencils and gives out $4 \times 15 = 60$. Then $144 - 60 = 84$ are left.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Which property shows that $(4 \times 7) \times 5 = 4 \times (7 \times 5)$?
questions.solution: The numbers stay in the same order and only the grouping changes, which is the associative property.

solve.work: Regrouping factors is the associative property.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the distributive property with $8 \times (100 - 2)$ to find $8 \times 98$.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Which statement explains why $2 \times (8 + 5)$ and $2 \times 8 + 5$ are not equal?
choices: In the first, the 2 is added to 8 and 5; in the second, it is multiplied.
In the first, the 2 multiplies only 8; in the second, both 8 and 5.
In the first, the 2 multiplies both 8 and 5; in the second, only 8.
Addition is always done before multiplication.
questions.answer: In the first, the 2 multiplies both 8 and 5; in the second, only 8.
questions.solution: In $2 \times (8 + 5)$ the parentheses make the 2 multiply the whole sum, so it equals $2 \times 13 = 26$. In $2 \times 8 + 5$ the 2 multiplies only 8, so it equals $16 + 5 = 21$.

solve.answer: In the first, the 2 multiplies both 8 and 5; in the second, only 8.
solve.work: In 2 x (8+5) the 2 multiplies both 8 and 5 (26); in 2 x 8 + 5 only the 8 (21).

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: What number makes $3 \times [? + (2 \times 5)] = 45$ true?
questions.solution: Since $3 \times 15 = 45$, the brackets equal 15. Then $? + 10 = 15$, so the ? is 5.

questions.skill: Equivalent expressions
questions.stem: Which expression has the same value as $3 \times (10 - 4)$?
questions.solution: $3 \times (10 - 4) = 3 \times 6 = 18$, and $3 \times 10 - 3 \times 4 = 30 - 12 = 18$. The others are 26, 14 and 43.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: A class of 28 students and 4 adults goes to a museum. They sit 8 people to a van. How many vans do they need?
questions.solution: There are $28 + 4 = 32$ people in all. Then $32 \div 8 = 4$ vans.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $3 \times [(18 - 6) \div 4 + 5]$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: Evaluate $[(9 + 6) \times 4] \div (12 - 7)$.
questions.solution: The bracket is $15 \times 4 = 60$ and the parentheses give $12 - 7 = 5$. $60 \div 5 = 12$.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with brackets and parentheses
questions.stem: Find the value of $50 - 2 \times [(7 + 3) + 5]$.
questions.solution: Inside the bracket: $10 + 5 = 15$. Multiply: $2 \times 15 = 30$. Subtract: $50 - 30 = 20$.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the properties of operations to find the value of $4 \times 17 \times 25$.
questions.solution: Multiply 4 and 25 first: $4 \times 25 = 100$. Then $100 \times 17 = 1{,}700$.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Use the distributive property to find the value of $7 \times 48 + 7 \times 52$.

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: What number makes $2 \times [? + (3 \times 4)] = 50$ true?
questions.solution: $50 \div 2 = 25$. Since $3 \times 4 = 12$, we need $? + 12 = 25$, so ? is 13.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: A florist makes 8 bouquets with 7 roses in each bouquet. She has 20 roses left over. How many roses did she have at first?
questions.solution: The bouquets use $8 \times 7 = 56$ roses. At first she had $56 + 20 = 76$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: A gym has 4 classes of 18 students and 2 classes of 25 students. How many students are in these classes in all?

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: A truck carries 9 boxes with 15 books in each box. After 47 books are unloaded, how many books are still on the truck?

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: Ida has 120 dollars. She buys 4 plants that cost 18 dollars each. How many dollars does she have left?
questions.solution: The plants cost $4 \times 18 = 72$ dollars. $120 - 72 = 48$.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: A bakery packs 144 muffins into boxes of 6. It sells 15 of the boxes. How many boxes are left?
questions.solution: $144 \div 6 = 24$ boxes. $24 - 15 = 9$ boxes left.

questions.skill: Find the missing number in an expression
questions.stem: What number makes $[? \div (2 + 4)] \times 5 = 20$ true?

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression shows "subtract 4 from the product of 6 and 5, then multiply by 3"?
questions.solution: The product $6 \times 5 = 30$, minus 4 gives 26, and then that whole result is multiplied by 3, so parentheses are needed.

questions.skill: Solve a two-step word problem with an expression
questions.stem: Ms. Ortiz buys 4 packs of 12 pencils and 3 packs of 8 pens. Which expression shows how many pencils and pens she buys in all?
questions.solution: Pencils: $4 \times 12 = 48$. Pens: $3 \times 8 = 24$. Total: 72.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Rose has 60 beads. She uses 24 beads and shares the rest equally among 3 friends. Which expression shows how many beads each friend gets?
questions.solution: The rest is $60 - 24 = 36$ beads, which is then divided by 3. Each friend gets 12.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Mia says $(30 - 6) \div 3$ and $30 - 6 \div 3$ have the same value. Which statement is correct?
choices: They are the same: both are 8.
They are different: the first is 8 and the second is 28.
They are the same: both are 28.
They are different: the first is 28 and the second is 8.
questions.answer: They are different: the first is 8 and the second is 28.
questions.solution: First: $24 \div 3 = 8$. Second: division comes before subtraction, so $30 - 2 = 28$.

solve.answer: They are different: the first is 8 and the second is 28.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without evaluating
questions.stem: Which expression is 3 less than twice the sum of 14 and 6?
questions.solution: Twice the sum is $2 \times (14 + 6)$, and 3 less means subtract 3 from it.

questions.skill: Equivalent expressions
questions.stem: Which expression is NOT equal to $8 \times 15$?
questions.solution: $8 \times 15 = 120$. The expression $8 \times 10 + 5$ is 85, because the 8 does not multiply the 5.

questions.skill: Equivalent expressions
questions.stem: Which expression equals $12 \times 25$ when 12 is written as $3 \times 4$?
questions.solution: $3 \times (4 \times 25) = 3 \times 100 = 300 = 12 \times 25$.

questions.skill: Use properties of operations
questions.stem: Rosa wrote $7 \times 28 = 7 \times 30 - 7 \times 2$. Which idea did she use?
choices: The associative property, with 28 written as 30 - 2
The distributive property, with 28 written as 30 + 2
The commutative property, with 7 and 28 swapped
The distributive property, with 28 written as 30 - 2
questions.answer: The distributive property, with 28 written as 30 - 2
questions.solution: She wrote 28 as $30 - 2$ and multiplied 7 by each part, which is the distributive property. Both sides equal 196.

solve.answer: The distributive property, with 28 written as 30 - 2
